The four crossing edges give precisely the cyclic vertices. The two disjoint-edge barycentric decompositions of their diagonal intersection yield the positive normalized quadruple and recover both endpoints on each diagonal, so the inverse is unique. The reciprocal signed margin vanishes at those four points with the required signs.

Both triangles use the same base AC. Along BD, signed distance to AC varies linearly and changes sign, so the complementary area coefficient expresses e on BD. Combining the area-weighted centroids gives both stated forms of λ.

In Cartesian standard coordinates, computed the third cross-product components as ps/[(p+r)(q+s)] and qr(p+s)/[(p+r)(q+s)(q+r)]. Their common direction is perpendicular to the section and its normal has third component −p−s. The area-to-volume-and-gradient quotient is affine invariant, and triangle area ratios are preserved on the fixed plane.

The section and the triangle v₁CD are the cap faces away from v₀. Pyramids from v₀ give pα, pδ and q²/[(q+r)(q+s)]. All denominators are positive at repeated heights. Substitution yields α+δ=xyzw/Δ, y+(x+z)(x+w)=P−a+b, and the complementary numerator sums to (a−b)²+aR+bP. Since m(λ)=0 and m(g)=(p+q−r−s)/4, the signed moment agrees.

The distinct-height sum reduces to the raw fraction on clearing denominators. Independently evaluated exact vertex determinants and triangle areas on rational examples with distinct and repeated heights and checked the cap, coarea and Δ identities on 256 positive rational diagonal quadruples.

dependencies.mapping: Set d=3 and c=(p,q,-r,-s) with p,q,r,s>0, supplying at least two positive and at least one negative coefficient even when same-side heights repeat. The normalized exponentials are uniform in barycentric coordinates, so the signs of c·E and c·U give the same cap fraction F. The accepted proof gives 3 f_V(0)=f_{c·U}(0), which is S by linear coarea on T, and its section centroid b is the actual λ under affine transport.

overlap.comparison: Its proper-cut variation gives ∂F/∂tᵢ=Sλᵢ by taking x=−t and the level zero. It gives general derivative identities and does not evaluate the tetrahedral 2–2 geometry.
Its centroid derivative specializes exactly as recorded in the dependency. It supplies neither the diagonal bijection nor the cap, centroid, coarea and moment in diagonal coordinates.

The projection-tail divided difference proved there gives the distinct-height sum on taking d=3 and a positively rescaled shift of the four raw heights with the level shifted accordingly. It does not give the reciprocal-diagonal parametrization, the geometric formulas for the centroid and coarea, or the explicit moment.
